deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Must be set to PREVENT in order to stop accidental or malicious deletion of the instance using terraform

description.description: An optional description of this resource.
description.rationale: Only used to provide information describing the resource thus does not have security relations

name.description:
Name of the resource. The name must be 1-63 characters long and match
the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which means the
first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following
characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last
character, which cannot be a dash.
name.rationale: Only used for naming conventions and does not have impact on the security of the service

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Only used for identication purposes thus would not have an effect on the security of the resource

target.description: URL of the managed instance group that this autoscaler will scale.
target.rationale: Used to designate the target for the autoscaling thus would not have impact on security

zone.description: URL of the zone where the instance group resides.
zone.rationale: Should be set to a zone in which the instance is in to abide by data residency

autoscaling_policy.description:
The configuration parameters for the autoscaling algorithm. You can
define one or more of the policies for an autoscaler: cpuUtilization,
customMetricUtilizations, and loadBalancingUtilization.

If none of these are specified, the default will be to autoscale based
on cpuUtilization to 0.6 or 60%.

autoscaling_policy.cooldown_period.description:
The number of seconds that the autoscaler should wait before it
starts collecting information from a new instance. This prevents
the autoscaler from collecting information when the instance is
initializing, during which the collected usage would not be
reliable. The default time autoscaler waits is 60 seconds.

Virtual machine initialization times might vary because of
numerous factors. We recommend that you test how long an
instance may take to initialize. To do this, create an instance
and time the startup process.
autoscaling_policy.cooldown_period.rationale: Dictates the period of time for the collection of data from instances, thus too low of a cooldown period can lead to resource stability issues and compromise data

autoscaling_policy.max_replicas.description:
The maximum number of instances that the autoscaler can scale up
to. This is required when creating or updating an autoscaler. The
maximum number of replicas should not be lower than minimal number
of replicas.
autoscaling_policy.max_replicas.rationale: Too large of a max replicas value can negatively affect stability of service or can cause resource to crash thus comprimised the security

autoscaling_policy.min_replicas.description:
The minimum number of replicas that the autoscaler can scale down
to. This cannot be less than 0. If not provided, autoscaler will
choose a default value depending on maximum number of instances
allowed.
autoscaling_policy.min_replicas.rationale: Setting the minimum replicas to 0 would prevent the use of this service, thus this setting can be used maliciously

autoscaling_policy.mode.description: Defines operating mode for this policy.
autoscaling_policy.mode.rationale: Must be set intentionally and blacklist OFF as it can be used to maliciously stop the service from working.

autoscaling_policy.stabilization_period.description:
The number of seconds that the autoscaler waits for load stabilization
before making scale-in decisions.

This might appear as a delay in scaling in but it is an important mechanism
for your application to not have fluctuating size due to short term load
fluctuations.
autoscaling_policy.stabilization_period.rationale: Value chooses the period of time for load stabilization thus must be set to a resonable value to prevent stability issues and malicious attacks

autoscaling_policy.cpu_utilization.description:
Defines the CPU utilization policy that allows the autoscaler to
scale based on the average CPU utilization of a managed instance
group.

autoscaling_policy.cpu_utilization.predi.description:
Indicates whether predictive autoscaling based on CPU metric is enabled. Valid values are:

- NONE (default). No predictive method is used. The autoscaler scales the group to meet current demand based on real-time metrics.

- OPTIMIZE_AVAILABILITY. Predictive autoscaling improves availability by monitoring daily and weekly load patterns and scaling out ahead of anticipated demand.
autoscaling_policy.cpu_utilization.predi.rationale: Only used as method of prediction of autoscaling depending on the CPU metric, thus would not affect the security of the resource

autoscaling_policy.cpu_utilization.targe.description:
The target CPU utilization that the autoscaler should maintain.
Must be a float value in the range (0, 1]. If not specified, the
default is 0.6.

If the CPU level is below the target utilization, the autoscaler
scales down the number of instances until it reaches the minimum
number of instances you specified or until the average CPU of
your instances reaches the target utilization.

If the average CPU is above the target utilization, the autoscaler
scales up until it reaches the maximum number of instances you
specified or until the average utilization reaches the target
utilization.
autoscaling_policy.cpu_utilization.targe.rationale: Purpose is to choose the target CPU utilization is needed for the autoscaler, thus is more configuration and does not affect security aspects

autoscaling_policy.load_balancing_utiliz.description: Configuration parameters of autoscaling based on a load balancer.

Fraction of backend capacity utilization (set in HTTP(s) load
balancing configuration) that autoscaler should maintain. Must
be a positive float value. If not defined, the default is 0.8.
autoscaling_policy.load_balancing_utiliz.rationale: Used to set the backend capacity utilization thus would not affect the security properties and is more configuration

autoscaling_policy.metric.description: Configuration parameters of autoscaling based on a custom metric.

autoscaling_policy.metric.filter.description:
A filter string to be used as the filter string for
a Stackdriver Monitoring TimeSeries.list API call.
This filter is used to select a specific TimeSeries for
the purpose of autoscaling and to determine whether the metric
is exporting per-instance or per-group data.

You can only use the AND operator for joining selectors.
You can only use direct equality comparison operator (=) without
any functions for each selector.
You can specify the metric in both the filter string and in the
metric field. However, if specified in both places, the metric must
be identical.

The monitored resource type determines what kind of values are
expected for the metric. If it is a gce_instance, the autoscaler
expects the metric to include a separate TimeSeries for each
instance in a group. In such a case, you cannot filter on resource
labels.

If the resource type is any other value, the autoscaler expects
this metric to contain values that apply to the entire autoscaled
instance group and resource label filtering can be performed to
point autoscaler at the correct TimeSeries to scale upon.
This is called a per-group metric for the purpose of autoscaling.

If not specified, the type defaults to gce_instance.

You should provide a filter that is selective enough to pick just
one TimeSeries for the autoscaled group or for each of the instances
(if you are using gce_instance resource type). If multiple
TimeSeries are returned upon the query execution, the autoscaler
will sum their respective values to obtain its scaling value.
autoscaling_policy.metric.filter.rationale: Purpose is to set the TimeSeries for autoscaling configuration, thus does not affect security aspects

autoscaling_policy.metric.name.description:
The identifier (type) of the Stackdriver Monitoring metric.
The metric cannot have negative values.

The metric must have a value type of INT64 or DOUBLE.
autoscaling_policy.metric.name.rationale: Used to set the identifier for the Stackdriver Monitoring metric which does not have an effect of the security of the service

autoscaling_policy.metric.single_instanc.description:
If scaling is based on a per-group metric value that represents the
total amount of work to be done or resource usage, set this value to
an amount assigned for a single instance of the scaled group.
The autoscaler will keep the number of instances proportional to the
value of this metric, the metric itself should not change value due
to group resizing.

For example, a good metric to use with the target is
'pubsub.googleapis.com/subscription/num_undelivered_messages'
or a custom metric exporting the total number of requests coming to
your instances.

A bad example would be a metric exporting an average or median
latency, since this value can't include a chunk assignable to a
single instance, it could be better used with utilization_target
instead.
autoscaling_policy.metric.single_instanc.rationale: Used for the autoscaler interpret the workload metric dependent on the amount instances thus is it more related to configuration depending on the capacity thus is not directly related to the security aspects

autoscaling_policy.metric.target.description:
The target value of the metric that autoscaler should
maintain. This must be a positive value. A utilization
metric scales number of virtual machines handling requests
to increase or decrease proportionally to the metric.

For example, a good metric to use as a utilizationTarget is
www.googleapis.com/compute/instance/network/received_bytes_count.
The autoscaler will work to keep this value constant for each
of the instances.
autoscaling_policy.metric.target.rationale: Purpose is to define the target utilization to create and delete instances thus is configuration and not related to security properties

autoscaling_policy.metric.type.description:
Defines how target utilization value is expressed for a
Stackdriver Monitoring metric. Possible values: ["GAUGE", "DELTA_PER_SECOND", "DELTA_PER_MINUTE"]
autoscaling_policy.metric.type.rationale: Used to choose the format in which the target utilization value is interpreted in thus would not affect the security of the resource

autoscaling_policy.scale_in_control.description:
Defines scale in controls to reduce the risk of response latency
and outages due to abrupt scale-in events

autoscaling_policy.scale_in_control.time.description:
How long back autoscaling should look when computing recommendations
to include directives regarding slower scale down, as described above.
autoscaling_policy.scale_in_control.time.rationale: Must be set to a resonably higher value to prevent a window in which the resource can crash and be vunerable due to too short of a scale down window

autoscaling_policy.scale_in_control.max_.description:
Specifies a fixed number of VM instances. This must be a positive
integer.
autoscaling_policy.scale_in_control.max_.rationale: Must be configured as without configuration it can be used maliciously to remove instances during scale in events thus impact security of resource

autoscaling_policy.scale_in_control.max_.description:
Specifies a percentage of instances between 0 to 100%, inclusive.
For example, specify 80 for 80%.
autoscaling_policy.scale_in_control.max_.rationale: Chooses the perctage of instances that can be scaled in thus to improve stabily and prevent resource security vunerability it must not be set to too high of a percentage to prevent too agressive of a scale in

autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.description: Scaling schedules defined for an autoscaler. Multiple schedules can be set on an autoscaler and they can overlap.

autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.des.description: A description of a scaling schedule.
autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.des.rationale: Purpose is to provide descriptive information about the scaling schedule thus not security related

autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.dis.description: A boolean value that specifies if a scaling schedule can influence autoscaler recommendations. If set to true, then a scaling schedule has no effect.
autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.dis.rationale: Used to disable or enable the scaling schedule which controls the resource management, thus is configuration and not related to the security of the resource

autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.dur.description: The duration of time intervals (in seconds) for which this scaling schedule will be running. The minimum allowed value is 300.
autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.dur.rationale: Dictates how long the scaling schedule will run which is more configuration and would not have impact on security

autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.min.description: Minimum number of VM instances that autoscaler will recommend in time intervals starting according to schedule.
autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.min.rationale: Configuring the value to 0 would stop service from working thus, must be prevented in order to improve the services security from a malicious attack

autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.nam.rationale: A naming convention for the scaling schedule thus does not effect security properties

autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.sch.description: The start timestamps of time intervals when this scaling schedule should provide a scaling signal. This field uses the extended cron format (with an optional year field).
autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.sch.rationale: Purpose is to configure the times for scaling signal making it a configuration that does not effect the security aspects

autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.tim.description: The time zone to be used when interpreting the schedule. The value of this field must be a time zone name from the tz database: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tz_database.
autoscaling_policy.scaling_schedules.tim.rationale: Only purpose is for timezone interpretation and would not effect the data residency or security of service
